claims.text: Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states employee loans are granted under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 earnings call (June 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said there is a great platform with strength in all three channels, and that from the advisor-led side the firm does have recruiting, but it also has flows coming in from workplace.

Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q25 earnings call (March 2025), CEO Ted Pick said the firm is selective about recruiting, that the integrated firm offers unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology and compensation viewed to be fair and motivating, and that the firm is receiving a lot of inbound inquiry from advisors.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 earnings call (June 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said advisor-led flows were particularly strong, originating from new advisors attracted to the strength of the workplace, as well as assets that originated from workplace.
Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q25 earnings call (March 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said net new assets were supported by broad-based strength across channels, including positive recruiting trends.

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (December 2025), the firm said it is increasing the cash component of advisor compensation, changes that support the firm's overall investment into its financial advisors.

Merrill: On the 4Q25 earnings call (December 2025), management said Merrill is picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors, but this is not an enormous part of its strategy; the core is a training program to train people in wealth management at Bank of America and Merrill.
Merrill: On the 2Q25 earnings call (June 2025), management said Merrill and the Private Bank add financial advisors through an extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors.

Merrill: Trade press (November 16, 2026) reports Merrill largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf (who took over in 2023) restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.
Merrill: On the 1Q26 earnings call (March 2026), management said Merrill continues to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.

Merrill: The firm's recruiting page (content as of November 3, 2026) states Merrill recruits through its Advisor Development Program, which offers industry-leading training and dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses, and progresses participants through three roles until they graduate to Merrill Core Advisor.

Merrill: The firm's recruiting page (content as of November 3, 2026) pitches joining an iconic brand with infrastructure that supports lead generation through Bank of America's global bank, trust division and market presence.
Merrill: Trade press (September 11, 2026) reports Merrill is ramping up advisor recruiting efforts, adding advisors from rivals such as UBS, Morgan Stanley, Truist and Wells Fargo.

Merrill: On the 2Q26 earnings call (June 2026), management said both Merrill and the Private Bank continue to attract talented advisers drawn to the breadth of the platform and ability to deliver comprehensive solutions for clients.
Merrill: On the 3Q26 earnings call (September 2026), management said Merrill's ability to attract experienced advisers to the platform reflects strong demand for advice.
Merrill: On the 1Q25 earnings call (March 2025), management said Merrill incurred costs of hiring to add experienced advisors to the platform in Merrill and the Private Bank.

Raymond James Financial: On the 1Q26 earnings call (December 2025), management stated Raymond James would much rather recruit advisors one by one than make an acquisition, because it can then know the advisors are a good cultural fit and 100% of transition assistance paid goes to retention rather than to a seller.

Raymond James Financial: The fiscal 2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) attributes its ability to attract high-quality advisors to its values-based culture, commitment to service, and the unique ways it provides services to advisors.

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q25 earnings call (September 2025), the firm described its recruiting approach as a best-of-both-worlds value proposition combining an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions, and cited its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence as a differentiator.

Raymond James Financial: The firm's affiliation page (content as of April 21, 2026) states Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options under the name AdvisorChoice (Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, Corporate RIA), giving advisors the ability to match their professional goals to an affiliation option.

Raymond James Financial: On the 3Q26 earnings call (June 2026), the firm stated it leads its recruiting with culture and capabilities rather than the highest compensation check, while maintaining competitive economics and disciplined transition assistance.

Raymond James Financial: On the 1Q26 earnings call (December 2025), the firm described recruiting as a long-term, consistent process (a marathon, not a sprint) that requires ongoing investment, targeting advisors who want to be at the firm over the long term rather than those moving for the highest check.

Raymond James Financial: The 3Q26 10-Q (period ended June 30, 2026) states the firm offers loans to prospective financial advisors for recruiting (and retention) purposes, contingent on the individuals joining or continuing their affiliation and meeting conditions in their offer.

Raymond James Financial: On the 3Q26 earnings call (June 2026), the firm said it is agnostic as to how an advisor affiliates, offering the largest addressable market because it has all affiliation options at scale, and wants advisors to affiliate based on culture, values and platform.

Raymond James Financial: The fiscal 2025 10-K states the firm participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take when affiliating with a new firm and their ability to solicit prior-firm clients.

Morgan Stanley positions itself as selective, using an integrated-firm platform with intellectual capital and technology, and relies on deferred compensation as golden handcuffs for retention while not introducing retention bonuses in its 2027 pay plan. Merrill combines experienced-advisor recruiting (ramped back up after 2023) with an extensive Advisor Development Program for training new advisors, and reports attrition at near historic lows. Raymond James leads with culture and capabilities over the highest check, offers multiple affiliation options via AdvisorChoice, is disciplined on transition assistance, and cites a 97% advisor satisfaction rate and roughly 1% regretted attrition.
